research_question: Among 904 candidate rice lines, which single line has the highest measured 100-grain weight (GRWT100)?

input_data.selection_rule: top-20 by E1 predicted GRWT100 (argmax-probability under a Gaussian error model is monotone in prediction, so the top-20 predicted set maximizes P(true argmax measured within budget))

control_variables: same historical source panel as the model training data family.
execution_evidence: 20 separate query_evidence_oracle(candidate_id=...) calls, one per top-20 predicted line, returning {"candidate_id","measurement","evidence_type":"E3"}. uncertainty: All 20 queried lines came from one tail of the prediction distribution; the panel-level trait mean and sd are not directly observed. The 0.3 g margin of the top line over the runner-up exceeds the expected rounding error (0.05 g) but not the model's residual sd (~0.47 g).
conclusion: Real historical GRWT100 measurements for the 20 top-predicted lines. The highest measured value is IRIS_313.12254 = 5.0 g, which is also the model's rank-1 prediction. Runner-up IRIS_313.12349 = 4.7 g (model rank 14). Measured values range 2.8-5.0 (mean 3.61, sd 0.62). Rank agreement with prediction is positive (Spearman 0.473), so H1 is supported on both of its falsification clauses.
limitations: Only 20 of 904 lines measured, all from the extreme upper tail of predictions -> truncated sample

research_question: Given only 20 measurements among 904 candidates, how likely is it that an unmeasured candidate exceeds the observed maximum GRWT100 of 5.0 g?
control_variables: threshold fixed at the observed max 5.0 g
calibration parameters integrated over sampling error.
execution_evidence: Derived computation on ev-1 (E1 predictions) + ev-2 (E3 measurements): analysis/analyze.py and analysis/sensitivity.py in the run directory; OLS calibration, Monte Carlo over the (a,b) covariance (20,000 draws) and chi-square noise draws, plus a residual-sd sensitivity grid.
uncertainty: P(no exceed) reported as a range 0.93-1.00 driven mainly by residual-sd uncertainty; the point estimate from the 20 analysed pairs is 0.998.
conclusion: Calibration of E1 predictions to E3 measurements: measured = -8.10 + 3.49*pred (slope t=3.94), residual sd 0.465 g. Under this model the 884 unqueried lines have expected count above 5.0 g of ~0.00-0.08 and P(no unqueried line exceeds the observed 5.0 g) = 0.94-1.00, depending on the residual-sd assumption (0.47 -> ~1.00; 0.60 -> 0.997; 0.80 -> 0.93). The top risk unqueried line is IRIS_313.11705 (pred 3.171).
limitations: Calibration is extrapolated from a truncated (top-20 only) sample, so the slope and especially the residual sd are estimated over a narrow prediction range (3.17-3.66). Gaussian error and residual independence are assumptions
heavy tails or heteroscedasticity would raise the risk. Panel mean/sd of GRWT100 are not observed. The probability is therefore a model-based statement (E2), not a measured fact.

research_question: What are the real measured 100-grain weights of the top-20 model-ranked candidate lines?
control_variables: query set fixed a priori by model rank (no post-hoc selection).
execution_evidence: 20 query_evidence_oracle calls (10+10), each returning {"evidence_type":"E3","measurement":<float>}; values recorded verbatim in analysis_b3/calib.json.
uncertainty: Sampling error: each value is a single historical measurement rounded to 0.1 g; no replication or environment replication available.
conclusion: All 20 oracle queries (the full budget) were spent on the top-20 model-ranked lines. Measured GRWT100 ranged 2.8-5.0 g (mean 3.61, sd 0.60). Max = 5.0 g at IRIS_313.12254 (model rank 1). Runner-ups: IRIS_313.12349 4.7 (model rank 14), IRIS_313.12344 4.6 (rank 3), IRIS_313.12242 4.5 (rank 2).
limitations: the measured max is the max of a 20-line sample, not provably the pool max. One measurement per line, no replication, values rounded to 0.1 g.

research_question: Is the measured maximum of the queried top-20 likely to be the global maximum of the 904-candidate pool?
model: post-hoc calibration of rice_gs predictions on 20 real measurements
control_variables: Calibration fitted only on the 20 pre-registered queried lines
prediction range 3.17-3.66 g kept explicit as the support of the fit.
execution_evidence: analysis_b3/analyze.py and analysis_b3/sensitivity.py (python3.12 -I); outputs analysis_b3/calib.json plus printed sensitivity grid.
uncertainty: The posterior exceedance probability ranges from ~0.72 to ~1.00 depending on residual tail assumptions; it is E2 (model-based), not a measured quantity.
conclusion: Across the 20 queried lines, Spearman(predicted, measured) = +0.473 (p=0.035) and Pearson = 0.680, so H1's refutation clause (Spearman <= 0) did not trigger, and the model rank-1 line held the measured maximum. Calibration meas = -8.10 + 3.489*pred (slope s.e. 0.886, p=0.001; residual sd 0.442 g). Extrapolating this calibration to the 884 unqueried lines, the highest calibrated mean among unqueried lines is 2.96 g (pred 3.171), 2.04 g below the observed max. Posterior P(no unqueried line exceeds 5.0 g) is 0.999+ under a Gaussian residual model (sd 0.44-0.55), 0.983 at sd 0.70, and 0.72-0.90 under heavy-tailed Student-t residuals (df 4-8, sd 0.6). Expected number of unqueried exceedances is 0.000-0.33.
limitations: The calibration is extrapolated from a truncated top-of-pool sample (predictions span only 3.17-3.66 g), so slope, intercept and residual sd are themselves uncertain

the exceedance probability is model-based (E2), not measured. The linear fit gives negative means at the lowest predictions, which is unphysical and shows the fit is valid only near the sampled prediction range.
